text:
Predicates:
Employees(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
InCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemotelyFromHome(x) ::: x is working remotely from home.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in other countries.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James (constant).
Premises:
∀x (Employees(x) ∧ SchedulesMeeting(x, y) → InCompanyToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule meetings with customers appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees have lunch either in the company or at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x) → RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: All employees in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ InCompanyToday(james)) ∨ (¬Manager(james) ∧ ¬InCompanyToday(james)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
InCompanyToday(james) ::: James has lunch in the company.
